To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mouse sperm nuclei contain polypeptides of molecular weight 67, 69 and 63 kD that are homologues of somatic cell lamina polypeptide 67, 68 and 63, respectively, and that the absence of somatic cell polypeptide 68 from the sperm nuclei suggests that the sperm lamina is composed of a different complement of polypeptides from that of the somatic cell lamins.
the sperm nucleus contains a protein complement that is distinct from that of somatic cell nuclei, yet includes proteins that have counterparts in somatic cell nuclei.

the sperm nuclear envelope is composed of a protein complement that is distinct from that of somatic cells and includes proteins that may be intrinisically nuclear, as well as proteins that are homologous to proteins of the nuclear envelope of somatic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and analysis of the proteins of the mouse sperm nucleus and their relationship to proteins of the nuclear envelope and matrix of somatic cell nuclei.
the proteins that are conserved in the sperm head and the somatic nucleus, and with the proteins that may be unique to the sperm head.
the identification of the proteins of the mouse sperm head, and their comparison with the corresponding proteins of somatic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sperm nuclear structure is composed of a number of polypeptides that are sperm- unique and a number that are common to the somatic nuclear envelope, the former being probably intrinsically nuclear and the latter probably extra-nuclear.

the nuclear matrix of the sperm nucleus contains polypeptides that are unique to the sperm nucleus, as well as polypeptides that have been identified in the nuclear matrix of somatic cells, including polypeptides characteristic of the nuclear envelope and the pore complex lamina.
the sperm head is composed of two sets of polypeptides, one of which is unique to sperm and the other is homologous with polypeptides of the nuclear envelope and matrix of somatic cell nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the sperm, the nuclear matrix is a structure of the sperm nucleus that is conserved in its organization during spermiogenesis and that, in its protein composition, it shows homology with the protein complement of the somatic cell nuclear matrix.
the sperm nucleus contains proteins that are sperm-specific and proteins that are shared with somatic cells.

the nuclear matrix of the mouse sperm head, which is the residue of decondensed chromosomal material, has a protein complement with a significant degree of similarity to that of the somatic nuclear matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sperm nuclear matrix contains a subset of proteins that are homologous to the nuclear matrix of somatic cells.
there is a significant degree of homology between the sperm nuclear matrix and the somatic cell nuclear matrix.

the nuclear matrix is a highly dynamic structure that is not only involved in DNA replication and gene expression, but also is important in nuclear envelope assembly, cell division, and the maintenance of the nuclear shape.
